chief_complaint: incidental painless lump in neck on ultrasound
hpi_details: A 41-year-old male presents to the clinic with incidental painless lump in neck on ultrasound. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks the lump might just be an inflamed lymph node left over from a cold he had a few weeks ago.
concerns: He is worried that the neck lump might turn out to be throat cancer like his uncle had.
expectations: He hopes to find out whether he needs a needle biopsy or if he can safely monitor it with another ultrasound.

available_results.value: 1.8 cm solid hypoechoic right-lobe nodule with smooth margins; no suspicious cervical lymph nodes

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Thyroid Nodule is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes checking TSH, performing ultrasound, and pursuing fine-needle aspiration if indicated for Thyroid Nodule, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

must_ask.say: Any trouble swallowing or voice changes?
Any family history of thyroid cancer?

history.answer: I was told I have a lump in my neck during a routine checkup ultrasound a couple of weeks ago, and lately I've also been feeling quite fatigued.
I didn't feel anything myself. It was picked up incidentally on a routine health screening ultrasound two weeks ago, and I haven't noticed any sudden growth since then.
The clinic doctor told me it is located on the lower right side of the front of my neck.
As far as I know, there is just that single spot in my neck. I haven't noticed any swollen bumps in my armpits or groin.
No, it does not hurt at all, even when I touch or press on it.
I haven't noticed it catching, but the screening doctor said neck lumps can move when you swallow or stick your tongue out.
No, eating meals doesn't cause any swelling, tightness, or pain around my neck or jaw.
No, I haven't had a recent cold, sore throat, dental problem, or any skin infections.
No, I haven't had any fevers, chills, or night sweats.
I've felt gradually more worn out and fatigued recently, but my body weight has stayed completely the same.
No, my voice has been completely normal with no hoarseness or vocal changes.
No, I can swallow food and liquids normally, and I haven't had any trouble breathing or feeling short of breath.
No, I don't have ear pain, a blocked nose, nosebleeds, or pain when I swallow.
No heart palpitations, no shakiness in my hands, and no problems handling heat or cold.
No, I have never had tuberculosis, and I haven't been in contact with anyone sick with it.
No, I never had any radiation treatments to my head or neck when I was a child.
No, I don't keep pets and haven't had any scratches or contact with cats or other animals.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or thyroid disease.
I've never had any operations and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I'm not taking any medications, over-the-counter pills, or supplements.
No, I don't have any allergies to medications or anything else.
I have never smoked in my life.
I drink socially, maybe one beer once or twice a month at dinner with coworkers.
I work as an office accountant and live with my wife and our son.
No one in my family has had thyroid cancer, thyroid nodules, or any endocrine diseases.
I was wondering if it's just a swollen lymph node from a bad cold I had a couple of weeks ago.
I'm terrified that this could be cancer, because my uncle had a neck growth that turned out to be malignant.
I hope you can tell me if I need a needle test on this lump or if we can just keep an eye on it.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.6 degrees Celsius, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Well-developed, alert male in no acute distress; no obvious neck asymmetry or visible mass on casual inspection.
No exophthalmos, lid lag, or conjunctival pallor; extraocular movements are full.
Oral mucosa is pink and moist; pharynx and tonsils are clear without erythema, exudates, or mucosal lesions.
No palpable cervical, submandibular, submental, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
A discrete, non-tender, firm nodule measuring approximately 1.5 to 2 cm is palpable in the lower right thyroid lobe that moves upward smoothly upon swallowing; no bruit auscultated.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without wheezes, crackles, or rhonchi.
No postural or resting tremor noted with outstretched hands.
